web_evidence.title: Leadership in Literature: The Caine Mutiny
web_evidence.note: The U.S. Naval Institute's structural discussion distinguishes the author's voice from Willie and notes that the novel frequently narrates events Willie could not have known, supporting an external omniscient narrator.

web_evidence.title: Herman Wouk Writing Styles in The Caine Mutiny
web_evidence.note: The Gale-derived study-guide analysis explicitly says that despite varied narrative techniques, the novel remains third-person omniscient.

web_evidence.title: The Caine Mutiny Analysis
web_evidence.note: This explicit style analysis identifies a third-person omniscient narrator that provides access to multiple characters' perspectives.

search_log: Searched "The Caine Mutiny Herman Wouk excerpt first chapter" and opening-chapter variants; chapter summaries and quoted passages showed external narration of Willie, but no sustained authorized excerpt was freely accessible.

Searched "The Caine Mutiny point of view third person narrator", "third-person omniscient", and narrator/omniscient variants; opened the U.S. Naval Institute, BookRags/Gale, SparkNotes, and eNotes results rather than relying on snippets.
Checked Google Books and Open Library editions; they verified the work and offered limited or preview-only access but did not expose enough contiguous prose to serve as Tier A evidence.

A Columbia search result exposed an extensively revised original-manuscript page proposing a first-person Willie framing; because it is draft manuscript material rather than the published text, and published-work analyses consistently describe external third-person narration, it was treated as a research dead end rather than contrary book evidence.
Checked the University of Pennsylvania Caine Mutiny Court-Martial excerpt, but it is a dramatic adaptation and therefore was not used to classify the novel's base narration.
person_note: The diagnostic Goodreads passages repeatedly use sustained external narration to report Willie's perceptions, thoughts, ignorance, and development, especially q00713, q00714, q00728, q00745, and q00751. First- and second-person forms elsewhere occur in dialogue or gnomic material and do not create alternate base sections. Two whole-book structural analyses independently identify an external omniscient authorial voice, with the Naval Institute specifically observing that it narrates events beyond Willie's knowledge; a third explicit source corroborates this. The inaccessible authorized previews leave a minor coverage limitation, but the distributed interior quotations and multiple structural sources agree strongly on THIRD.
